newsitem.title: INDIA: Mere cosmetic changes seen to sour Indian bourses.
newsitem.headline: Mere cosmetic changes seen to sour Indian bourses.

text.p: India's bubbling stock markets will take a beating if new measures promised by the government this week turn out to be merely cosmetic changes, brokers said on Wednesday.
"The market would react negatively," said Ramesh Damani, a member-broker at the Bombay Stock Exchange. "This is a choppy market driven by bouts of frenzy."

Market regulator the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) is scheduled to consider a stock lending scheme, an amendment in the country's share depository act, a report on short sales and a new takeover code, a SEBI official said.
People are hoping for tax breaks on company dividends, buy-back of shares by companies, easing carry-forward rules for stock markets and changes in a controversial minimum tax on firms.
But one broker said: "I'm very sceptical. The government has very little leeway -- it is caught between the rock and a hard place."
On Wednesday the benchmark Bombay Stock Exchange index fell 78.36 points, or 2.17 percent, to 3,525.84.
Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda had said on Monday that some decisions could be expected before he left on Friday for Davos in Switzerland to attend the World Economic Forum.
